amendments.what: the ridge is 0.01, not 1.0 (the first text of this declaration said 1.0, 'about one pseudo-day on a flag')
amendments.when: before any score: only unit tests on synthetic panels and the published panel's reserve reads had been run; no forecast of B4 had been compared with an outcome or with any other model
amendments.why: a unit test on a synthetic panel (a 15 bp quarter-end spike, nine flagged training pairs) showed that 1.0 in bp squared against a loss that is linear in the residual shrinks that effect from 15 bp to about 2 bp, which is not a 'small' ridge. The directive asks for a small fixed ridge; 0.01 keeps the normal equations stable and moves no effect below 75 bp by more than the sampling noise

amendments.what: the iteration stop is a coefficient move of 0.001, not 1e-6 (the first text said 1e-6)
amendments.when: before any score: timing and objective checks of single fits only, on the published panel's pairs as of 2023-11-08; no forecast of B4 had been compared with an outcome or with any other model
amendments.why: timing on the published panel showed that the reweighting converges slowly in the coefficients (about 90 of 100 iterations used at 1e-6) while the objective is flat: the loss at 100 iterations differed from the loss at 2,000 iterations by less than 0.01 on a total of 560 to 1,900, at three levels. A move of 0.001 bp stops the iteration where the loss no longer changes by 0.01 and saves a quarter of the time. The run reports how many fits stopped at the cap

amendments.what: B4 is walked over the decision days the candidate's walk forecast, not over the panel from its first row
amendments.when: before any score: the first run raised before any forecast was made
amendments.why: the first full run stopped at once: the panel's first decision days have no row whose target is observable (asof SplitError) and the candidate's walk skips them. The refit cadence ('the candidate's cadence') is counted from the first day each model forecasts, so B4 starts on the candidate's first forecast day and both refit on the same days. A scored decision day without a B4 forecast is still refused

label: development, not a verdict
reading_rules: A figure is a check on days that were already seen. Nothing here is a verdict, nothing is registered and no choice is made on it; the candidate stays (s3c-ann-net).
A pooled figure is never read without the lead, regime and day-type splits beside it.
Where B4 beats the candidate in a split, the page says so plainly; it is what the benchmark is for.
Whether B4 joins the decision rule is Eleonora's, as a marked question with numbered options and a default that changes no claim (reported beside; B1 stays the deciding benchmark).
